facts.fact: Soil types by unconfined compressive strength: Type A is cohesive soil of 1.5 tons per sq ft (tsf) or more; Type B is over 0.5 but under 1.5 tsf; Type C is 0.5 tsf or less. Fissured, vibrated or previously disturbed soil can't be Type A.
Excavated spoil, materials and equipment must be kept at least 2 ft back from the edge of an excavation, or held back by retaining devices.
Where an oxygen-deficient or hazardous atmosphere could exist, the air must be tested before workers enter excavations deeper than 4 ft.
A competent person must inspect excavations, adjacent areas and protective systems daily before work starts, as needed during the shift, and after every rainstorm or other hazard-increasing event.

Workers may not be inside a trench shield while it is being installed, removed or moved vertically. Digging up to 2 ft below the bottom of a shield is allowed only if the shield is rated for the full trench depth and no soil is being lost from behind or below it.
Walkways must be provided where people or equipment cross over excavations, and guardrails are required on walkways 6 ft or more above lower levels.
The estimated location of underground utilities (sewer, water, fuel, electric) must be determined before opening an excavation.
facts.note: Call 811 before digging.

facts.fact: A portable ladder used for access must extend at least 3 ft above the upper landing surface.
Gallons per foot of pipe = 0.0408 x (inside diameter in inches) squared. Examples: 2 in = 0.163 gal/ft; 3 in = 0.367 gal/ft; 4 in = 0.653 gal/ft; 6 in = 1.469 gal/ft.
facts.note: Derived from (0.7854 x d squared x 12) / 231.

facts.fact: One cubic foot holds 7.48 gallons, and one gallon is 231 cubic inches.
Water weighs about 8.34 lb per gallon and 62.4 lb per cubic foot.
Each foot of water height (head) creates 0.433 psi of pressure, and 1 psi lifts water 2.31 ft. Example: a 50 ft column of water exerts 50 x 0.433 = 21.65 psi at the bottom.
Worked example: with 60 psi static pressure at the street and a fixture 30 ft above it, static pressure at the fixture = 60 - (30 x 0.433) = 60 - 13 = about 47 psi, before friction loss.
For a 45-degree offset, travel = offset x 1.414 and run (setback) = offset x 1.000. Example: a 24 in offset needs about 33.9 in of travel, center to center.
Offset multipliers (travel / run): 60 degrees = 1.155 / 0.577; 30 degrees = 2.000 / 1.732; 22-1/2 degrees = 2.613 / 2.414; 11-1/4 degrees = 5.126 / 5.027.

For a rolling offset, first find the true offset = square root of (rise squared + roll squared), then multiply the true offset by the fitting constant (1.414 for 45-degree fittings) to get the travel. Example: rise 12 in, roll 9 in gives a true offset of 15 in and a 45-degree travel of 21.2 in.
Percent grade = fall / run x 100. 1/4 in per ft = 0.25/12 = 2.08% (about 2%); 1/8 in per ft = 1.04% (about 1%); 1/16 in per ft = 0.52%.
Total fall = slope x length. Example: 60 ft of pipe at 1/4 in per ft falls 15 in. 80 ft at 1/8 in per ft falls 10 in.
Rectangular tank volume = length x width x height (in feet) x 7.48 for gallons. Example: 4 ft x 3 ft x 2 ft = 24 cu ft = about 179.5 gallons.
Cylindrical tank volume = 0.7854 x diameter squared x height (in feet), then x 7.48 for gallons. Example: 2 ft diameter x 5 ft tall = 15.7 cu ft = about 117.5 gallons.
Area of a circle = 0.7854 x diameter squared (or pi x r squared). Because area grows with the square of the diameter, a 4 in pipe has four times the cross-sectional area of a 2 in pipe.
Worked example: 100 ft of 4 in pipe holds 100 x 0.653 = 65.3 gallons, which weighs about 65.3 x 8.34 = 545 lb when full of water.

Linear pipe expansion: change in length = coefficient x length x temperature change. Roughly, copper grows about 1.1 in per 100 ft per 100 F, and PVC about 3.6 in per 100 ft per 100 F (plastic pipe expands about three times as much as copper).
facts.note: Coefficients are approximate and vary by source (copper about 9.4 to 9.8 x 10^-6, PVC about 3.0 x 10^-5 in/in/F).

facts.fact: 1 in of water column = 0.036 psi, and 1 psi = 27.7 in of water column. 1 ft of head = 0.433 psi.
Under the UPC, a shower compartment needs at least 1,024 sq in of interior floor area and must be able to contain a 30 in circle. The IPC requires only 900 sq in.
facts.note: Confirmed via the 2022 California Plumbing Code (based on UPC 2021).

facts.fact: Under the UPC, a water closet or bidet must be at least 15 in from its center to a side wall or obstruction and 30 in center to center from a similar fixture, with at least 24 in of clear space in front. The IPC requires 21 in in front.

UPC maximum trap arm lengths (at 1/4 in per ft): 1-1/4 in = 2 ft 6 in; 1-1/2 in = 3 ft 6 in; 2 in = 5 ft; 3 in = 6 ft; 4 in = 10 ft. The vent may not be closer than two pipe diameters from the trap weir. These are much shorter than IPC Table 909.1.
facts.note: Values confirmed in the 2018 UPC table, unchanged in 2021.

facts.fact: Under the UPC, horizontal drainage piping normally slopes at least 1/4 in per ft (2%). Pipe 4 in and larger may slope 1/8 in per ft (1%) only where the authority having jurisdiction approves because 1/4 in per ft is impractical. The IPC allows 1/8 in per ft for 3 in to 6 in pipe outright.

UPC vent terminals must extend at least 6 in above the roof and be at least 1 ft from any vertical surface. They must be at least 10 ft from, or 3 ft above, any openable window, door, opening, air intake or vent shaft, and at least 3 ft from a lot line (alleys and streets excepted).
Under the UPC, a domestic clothes washer on a 2 in standpipe is rated 3 DFU. The IPC rates a residential clothes washer at 2 DFU.

UPC tests match the IPC on the main numbers: DWV water test with at least a 10 ft head for 15 minutes; DWV air test at 5 psi (or 10 in of mercury) for 15 minutes; water supply test at working pressure, or 50 psi air for non-plastic pipe, for 15 minutes.

Under the UPC, a cleanout is required at the upper end of each horizontal drain and at least every 100 ft. An extra cleanout is required for each aggregate horizontal change of direction exceeding 135 degrees, instead of the IPC's 45-degree / 40-ft rule.
facts.note: Confirmed only in a source describing the 2009 UPC. Check UPC 2021 707.4.

facts.fact: UPC cleanout clearance: at least 12 in in front of cleanouts on pipes 2 in and smaller, and 18 in for larger pipes.
facts.note: Confirmed only in a source describing the 2009 UPC. Check UPC 2021 707.9.

facts.fact: UPC clothes washer standpipes must extend at least 18 in but no more than 30 in above the trap weir. The IPC allows up to 42 in.
facts.note: Recalled but not confirmed in a source this round.

facts.fact: Under the UPC, water pipe may share a trench with a building sewer of clay or other materials not approved for use inside a building only if the bottom of the water pipe is at least 12 in above the top of the sewer and the water pipe sits on a solid shelf at least 12 in horizontally from the sewer.
facts.note: Recalled UPC text. Not confirmed this round.

facts.fact: Some UPC-based codes (for example, California) require water closets to average no more than 1.28 gallons per flush, compared with the IPC's 1.6 gpf.
facts.note: California's 1.28 gpf rule (CPC 411.2) is confirmed. Whether the base UPC 2021 body requires 1.28 or 1.6 gpf was not confirmed.

questions.q: Under the IPC, a DWV rough-in water test requires at least what head of water, held for how long?
questions.why: The DWV water test uses at least a 10 ft head held for at least 15 minutes.

questions.q: What pressure is used for an IPC DWV air test?
questions.why: The air test is 5 psi or enough to balance a 10 in mercury column, held 15 minutes.

questions.q: Under the IPC, which piping may NOT be tested with air?
questions.why: The IPC prohibits air testing of plastic piping.

questions.q: An air test of a non-plastic water supply system must be at least:
questions.why: Water supply systems are tested at working pressure with water, or at 50 psi with air for non-plastic pipe, for 15 minutes.

questions.q: A forced (pumped) sewer is tested at what pressure?
c: 5 psi greater than the pump rating
questions.why: Forced sewers are tested at least 5 psi above the pump rating for 15 minutes.

questions.q: How deep must water be at the threshold when testing a site-built shower liner?
questions.why: The liner is filled to at least 2 in deep at the threshold and held 15 minutes.

questions.q: How often must testable backflow assemblies such as RPZs be tested after installation?
questions.why: They are tested at installation, after repair or relocation, and at least once a year.

questions.q: The manometer final test of a DWV system requires holding what water column for 15 minutes?
questions.why: The final test requires at least a 1 in water column held for 15 minutes.

questions.q: Maximum horizontal support spacing for PVC DWV pipe under the IPC is:
questions.why: PVC and ABS need horizontal support every 4 ft.

questions.q: Maximum horizontal hanger spacing for 1/2 in PEX tubing is:
questions.why: PEX 1 in and smaller is supported every 32 in (2.67 ft) horizontally.

questions.q: Copper tubing 1 in in diameter must be supported horizontally at least every:
questions.why: Copper tubing 1-1/4 in and smaller is supported every 6 ft horizontally.

questions.q: Hubless cast-iron pipe in 5 ft lengths needs horizontal support at least every:
questions.why: Cast iron is supported every 5 ft (10 ft only where 10 ft lengths are installed).

questions.q: Sway bracing is required at changes in direction greater than 45 degrees for pipe sizes of:
questions.why: Rigid sway bracing is required for 4 in and larger pipe at changes over 45 degrees.

questions.q: A sleeve for a pipe through a foundation wall must be how much larger than the pipe?
questions.why: The sleeve must be two pipe sizes larger than the pipe passing through it.

questions.q: Steel shield plates protecting concealed pipe must be at least what thickness?
questions.why: Shield plates are at least 0.0575 in (No. 16 gauge) steel where pipe is within 1-1/2 in of the framing edge.

questions.q: Trench backfill is placed and tamped in layers of what thickness until the pipe crown is covered by 12 in?
questions.why: Loose earth is placed in 6 in layers and tamped until 12 in of tamped earth covers the crown.

questions.q: A tunnel for pipe installation is limited in length to one-half the trench depth, with a maximum of:
questions.why: Tunnels need 2 ft clear height above the pipe and are limited to half the trench depth, 8 ft maximum.

questions.q: A trench parallel to a footing may not extend into the bearing plane, a line projected downward from the footing's outside bottom edge at:
questions.why: The bearing plane slopes down at 45 degrees from the outside bottom edge of the footing.

questions.q: Exterior water supply piping must be installed at least how far below the frost line?
questions.why: It must be at least 6 in below the frost line and at least 12 in below grade.

questions.q: Under the IPC, the building drain extends to what point outside the building wall, where the building sewer begins?
questions.why: The building drain ends 30 in outside the exterior wall.

questions.q: A branch interval is roughly one story in height but never less than:
questions.why: A branch interval is not less than 8 ft.

questions.q: Under the IPC, a pipe installed at 30 degrees from horizontal is classified as:
questions.why: Pipe at less than 45 degrees from horizontal is horizontal.

questions.q: What is the temperature range of tempered water?
questions.why: The IPC defines tempered water as 85 F to 110 F.

questions.q: A capped branch is considered a dead end when its developed length is at least:
questions.why: A dead end is a closed branch 2 ft or more in developed length.

questions.q: Which of these is gray water under the IPC?
questions.why: Gray water comes from lavatories, bathtubs, showers, clothes washers and laundry trays.

questions.q: Minimum clearance from the center of a water closet to a side wall under the IPC:
questions.why: Water closets must be at least 15 in from center to any side wall or obstruction.

questions.q: Minimum clear space in front of a water closet under the IPC:
questions.why: The IPC requires 21 in in front. The UPC requires 24 in.

questions.q: Minimum size of a water closet compartment for a floor-mounted water closet:
questions.why: Floor-mounted: 30 x 60 in. Wall-hung: 30 x 56 in.

questions.q: Minimum interior area of a shower compartment under the IPC:
questions.why: IPC showers need 900 sq in with a 30 in minimum dimension.

questions.q: A shower with a 25 in minimum dimension is allowed under the IPC only if its area is at least:
questions.why: The exception allows a 25 in minimum dimension with at least 1,300 sq in.

questions.q: A site-built shower liner must turn up at least how far above the finished threshold?
questions.why: Liners turn up at least 2 in above the threshold and slope 1/4 in per ft to the drain.

questions.q: Minimum thickness of a PVC sheet shower liner:
questions.why: PVC and CPE liners must be at least 0.040 in (40 mil).

questions.q: In an assembly or educational occupancy, urinals may be substituted for up to what percentage of required water closets?
questions.why: Up to 67% in assembly and educational occupancies; 50% in others.

questions.q: The maximum hot water temperature an individual shower valve may be set to deliver is:
questions.why: The installer sets the limit stop so outlet water does not exceed 120 F.

questions.q: Maximum water temperature supplied to a bidet:
questions.why: Bidet water is limited to 110 F by an ASSE 1070 device.

questions.q: Minimum waste outlet diameter for a lavatory:
questions.why: Lavatory waste outlets must be at least 1-1/4 in.

questions.q: Minimum outlet size for a floor drain:
questions.why: Floor drains need at least a 2 in outlet.

questions.q: A fixture with concealed slip joints needs an access opening at least how large in its smallest dimension?
questions.why: The access panel or utility space must be at least 12 in in its smallest dimension.

questions.q: Maximum flow rate for a showerhead under the IPC:
questions.why: Showerheads are limited to 2.5 gpm at 80 psi.

questions.q: Separate men's and women's facilities are not required in a building whose total occupant load is no more than:
questions.why: Separate facilities aren't required where the total occupant load is 15 or fewer.

questions.q: Mercantile water closet ratio in Table 403.1:
questions.why: Mercantile needs 1 water closet per 500 occupants.

questions.q: Maximum path of travel to required toilet facilities (outside malls):
questions.why: Travel distance may not exceed 500 ft (300 ft in malls).

questions.q: An ADA water closet centerline must be how far from the side wall?
questions.why: The accessible water closet centerline is 16 in minimum to 18 in maximum from the side wall.

questions.q: Accessible water closet seat height (to top of seat):
questions.why: Seat height is 17 in to 19 in above the floor.

questions.q: Grab bars must be mounted at what height to the top of the gripping surface?
questions.why: Grab bars are mounted 33 in to 36 in above the floor.

questions.q: Maximum rim height of an accessible lavatory:
questions.why: The rim or counter surface may be no higher than 34 in.

questions.q: A water heater relief valve may be set no higher than the heater's rated working pressure or:
questions.why: The relief valve setting is limited to the rated working pressure or 150 psi, whichever is less.

questions.q: The temperature relief valve's sensing element must be in what part of the tank?
questions.why: The valve must respond to water in the top 6 in of the tank.

questions.q: Minimum depth of a water heater drain pan:
questions.why: Pans must be at least 1-1/2 in deep with a 3/4 in drain.

questions.q: Minimum diameter of a water heater pan drain:
questions.why: The pan drain is an indirect waste pipe at least 3/4 in in diameter.

questions.q: A pan drain run to the outdoors must end how far above the adjacent ground?
questions.why: Outdoor pan drains terminate 6 in to 24 in above grade.

questions.q: In a garage, a water heater's ignition source must be elevated at least:
questions.why: Ignition sources must be at least 18 in above the garage floor unless the heater is FVIR-listed.

questions.q: Which item is prohibited on water heater relief valve discharge piping?
questions.why: The discharge end may not be threaded; it also may not be trapped or have valves or tees.

questions.q: Under the UPC, where must seismic water heater straps be located?
c: Top and bottom 6 in of the tank
Upper third and lower third, lower strap 4 in above controls
Upper half, 12 in below the top
questions.why: UPC strapping is in the upper and lower thirds, with the lower strap at least 4 in above the controls.

questions.q: Minimum size of a water service pipe under the IPC:
questions.why: The water service must be at least 3/4 in.

questions.q: Minimum separation between the water service and building sewer (no exceptions applied):
c: 5 ft of undisturbed or compacted earth
questions.why: The water service and building sewer must be separated by at least 5 ft.

questions.q: Minimum fixture supply pipe size for a lavatory:
questions.why: A lavatory supply may be 3/8 in.

questions.q: Minimum fixture supply size for a flush-valve water closet:
questions.why: Flush-valve water closets need a 1 in supply.

questions.q: A water-hammer arrestor must comply with which standard?
questions.why: Water-hammer arrestors conform to ASSE 1010.

questions.q: Maximum weighted-average lead content for pipe and fittings supplying drinking water:
questions.why: Drinking water components must meet NSF 372 with no more than 0.25% weighted average lead.

questions.q: Under the IPC, which material is approved for underground water service but NOT for water distribution inside a building?
questions.why: PVC is a water service material only; it isn't listed for interior distribution.

questions.q: A booster pump low-pressure cutoff must stop the pump when suction pressure drops to:
questions.why: The low-pressure cutoff activates at 10 psi or less on the suction side.

questions.q: Maximum developed length of hot water piping from the source to a fixture:
questions.why: The IPC limits hot or tempered water piping to 50 ft from the source.

questions.q: When is a thermal expansion control device required on a storage water heater?
c: On every water heater regardless of system
When the cold supply passes through a check valve, PRV or backflow preventer
questions.why: A closed system created by a check valve, PRV or backflow preventer requires thermal expansion control.

questions.q: Which standard covers master thermostatic mixing valves installed at the water heater?
questions.why: Temperature-actuated mixing valves at the source comply with ASSE 1017.

questions.q: Which device protects against both back pressure and backsiphonage for a high-hazard connection?
questions.why: The RPZ handles back pressure and backsiphonage at high hazard.

questions.q: Which backflow device may NOT have a shutoff valve installed downstream of it?
questions.why: An AVB can't be under continuous pressure, so no downstream valves are allowed.

questions.q: An atmospheric vacuum breaker's critical level must be at least how far above the flood level rim or highest outlet?
questions.why: AVBs are installed with the critical level at least 6 in above the flood level rim.

questions.q: What is the minimum air gap for a lavatory faucet (effective opening up to 1/2 in) away from a wall?
questions.why: Lavatory air gap is 1 in away from walls, 1-1/2 in near a wall.

questions.q: How high must a barometric loop rise?
questions.why: A barometric loop must extend at least 35 ft high.

questions.q: A lawn irrigation system that injects fertilizer must be protected by:
questions.why: Where chemicals are introduced, an RPZ is required.

questions.q: Downstream piping from a carbonated beverage dispenser's backflow device must not be:
questions.why: CO2 forms carbonic acid that attacks copper; downstream piping must resist CO2.

questions.q: One approved disinfection method is a chlorine solution of at least 50 ppm held for:
questions.why: 50 ppm for 24 hours, or 200 ppm for 3 hours.

questions.q: Minimum slope for an 8 in horizontal drain under the IPC:
questions.why: Drains 8 in and larger may slope 1/16 in per ft.

questions.q: Horizontal branches must connect to the base of a stack at least how far downstream?
questions.why: Connections must be at least 10 stack diameters downstream.

questions.q: A sanitary tee is permitted for which change of direction?
questions.why: Sanitary tees are only for horizontal-to-vertical changes.

questions.q: DFU value of a private 1.6 gpf water closet:
questions.why: Private 1.6 gpf water closets are 3 DFU; public are 4.

questions.q: DFU value of a bathroom group with a 1.6 gpf water closet:
questions.why: A bathroom group is 5 DFU with a 1.6 gpf water closet and 6 DFU with a higher-flush one.

questions.q: DFU value of a residential clothes washer under the IPC:
questions.why: IPC: 2 DFU residential, 3 DFU commercial. The UPC rates a domestic washer at 3.

questions.q: Continuous flow into a drainage system is converted at:
questions.why: Each gpm of continuous flow counts as 2 DFU.

questions.q: Maximum DFU on a 4 in building drain at 1/4 in per ft:
questions.why: 4 in at 1/4 in per ft carries 216 DFU (180 at 1/8, 250 at 1/2).

questions.q: Maximum DFU on a 3 in building drain at 1/4 in per ft:
questions.why: 3 in at 1/4 in per ft carries 42 DFU.

questions.q: Maximum DFU on a 2 in horizontal fixture branch:
questions.why: A 2 in horizontal fixture branch carries 6 DFU.

questions.q: For a fixture not listed in Table 709.1 that has a 2 in trap, the DFU value is:
questions.why: Table 709.2 assigns 3 DFU to a 2 in trap or fixture drain.

questions.q: Maximum spacing of cleanouts on horizontal drains inside a building:
questions.why: Cleanouts are required at intervals of no more than 100 ft.

questions.q: Where a drain run has several changes of direction over 45 degrees, one cleanout is required for each:
questions.why: With multiple changes of direction, one cleanout per 40 ft of developed length.

questions.q: Required rodding clearance in front of a cleanout on a 4 in pipe:
questions.why: 18 in for 6 in and smaller pipe; 36 in for 8 in and larger.

questions.q: Minimum cleanout size on a 6 in drain:
questions.why: Cleanouts match pipe size up to 4 in; for larger pipe, at least 4 in.

questions.q: Minimum dimensions of a sump pit (unless otherwise approved):
questions.why: Sump pits are at least 18 in in diameter and 24 in deep.

questions.q: A sewage ejector receiving water closet discharge must pass spherical solids up to:
questions.why: Ejectors serving water closets handle 2 in solids; others handle 1 in.

questions.q: Minimum capacity of a sewage pump with a 2 in discharge:
questions.why: 2 in = 21 gpm, 2-1/2 in = 30 gpm, 3 in = 46 gpm.

questions.q: A backwater valve is required for fixtures on a floor lower than:
c: The next upstream public sewer manhole cover
questions.why: Fixtures below the upstream manhole cover elevation need backwater valve protection.

questions.q: An indirect waste pipe must be trapped when its horizontal developed length exceeds:
questions.why: Trap it when it exceeds 30 in horizontally or 54 in total developed length.

questions.q: A clothes washer standpipe must extend above its trap weir at least 18 in but not more than:
questions.why: IPC standpipes are 18 in to 42 in above the trap weir.

questions.q: Water above what temperature may not be discharged directly into the drainage system?
questions.why: Waste above 140 F must discharge to an indirect waste receptor.

questions.q: Vent systems must keep trap seals from being exposed to a pressure differential greater than:
questions.why: Trap seals may not see more than a 1 in water column pressure differential.

questions.q: A vent stack is required for every drainage stack with how many branch intervals or more?
questions.why: Drainage stacks with five or more branch intervals need a vent stack.

questions.q: A dry vent must rise vertically to at least how far above the flood level rim of the highest fixture before running horizontally?
questions.why: Dry vents rise at least 6 in above the flood level rim before going horizontal.

questions.q: Minimum size of any vent pipe under the IPC:
questions.why: Vents are at least half the drain diameter and never less than 1-1/4 in.

questions.q: A vent with more than what developed length must be increased one pipe size?
questions.why: Vents over 40 ft in developed length are increased one nominal size.

questions.q: Maximum trap-to-vent distance for a 1-1/2 in trap under the IPC:
questions.why: Table 909.1: 1-1/2 in trap = 6 ft at 1/4 in per ft.

questions.q: Maximum trap-to-vent distance for a 2 in trap under the IPC:
questions.why: Table 909.1: 2 in trap = 8 ft at 1/4 in per ft.

questions.q: A vent may not be installed within how many pipe diameters of the trap weir?
questions.why: Crown venting within two pipe diameters of the weir is prohibited.

questions.q: Maximum number of fixtures that may be circuit vented on one horizontal branch:
questions.why: A circuit vent may serve up to eight fixtures.

questions.q: Maximum slope of the vent section of a circuit-vented horizontal branch:
questions.why: The circuit-vented section may slope no more than 1 unit in 12 (8%).

questions.q: Maximum slope of a horizontal combination waste and vent pipe:
questions.why: Combination waste and vent piping may slope no more than 1/2 in per ft.

questions.q: A 2 in wet vent may carry a maximum of how many DFU?
questions.why: Wet vent sizes: 1-1/2 in = 1, 2 in = 4, 2-1/2 in = 6, 3 in = 12 DFU.

questions.q: Relief vents are required on soil and waste stacks having more than how many branch intervals?
questions.why: Stacks over 10 branch intervals need relief vents at every tenth interval.

questions.q: Individual and branch air admittance valves must be at least how far above the horizontal branch or fixture drain they vent?
questions.why: Branch AAVs: 4 in above the drain. Stack AAVs: 6 in above the highest flood rim.

questions.q: Individual and branch-type air admittance valves must comply with:
questions.why: ASSE 1051 covers individual and branch AAVs; ASSE 1050 covers stack-type.

questions.q: An open vent terminal within 10 ft horizontally of an operable window must be at least how far above the top of the window?
questions.why: Within 10 ft horizontally, the vent must be at least 3 ft above the opening.

questions.q: A sidewall vent terminal must be at least how far from a lot line?
questions.why: Through-wall vents are at least 10 ft from the lot line and 10 ft above average grade.

questions.q: Where a roof is used as a sun deck or promenade, vent pipes must extend at least how far above the roof?
questions.why: Vents on occupied roofs terminate at least 7 ft above the roof.

questions.q: Maximum vertical distance from a fixture outlet to the trap weir:
questions.why: Vertical distance is 24 in max; horizontal distance is 30 in max.

questions.q: Which trap is prohibited by the IPC?
questions.why: S-traps, bell traps, drum traps, crown-vented traps and moving-part traps are prohibited.

questions.q: One trap may serve a two-compartment sink if the compartments differ in depth by no more than:
questions.why: Compartments may differ by up to 6 in, with outlets no more than 30 in apart.

questions.q: An oil separator at a repair garage needs at least how much capacity for the first 100 sq ft drained?
questions.why: 6 cu ft for the first 100 sq ft plus 1 cu ft per additional 100 sq ft.

questions.q: Commercial laundry interceptors must stop solids of at least what size?
questions.why: The basket must stop solids 1/2 in or larger.

questions.q: Storm drainage is sized using which rainfall rate?
questions.why: IPC storm sizing uses the 100-year hourly rainfall rate.

questions.q: When a vertical wall drains onto a roof, what portion of the wall area is added to the roof area?
questions.why: Add one-half the wall area to the projected roof area.

questions.q: Each gpm of continuous flow into a storm drain equals how much roof area?
questions.why: 1 gpm = 24 sq ft of roof area based on 4 in/hr rainfall.

questions.q: Minimum opening dimension of a secondary (overflow) scupper:
questions.why: Scuppers may not have any opening dimension under 4 in.

questions.q: Minimum diameter of a subsoil drain:
questions.why: Subsoil drains must be at least 4 in in diameter.

questions.q: Minimum test pressure for a fuel gas piping system:
c: 1-1/2 times working pressure, not less than 3 psig
2 times working pressure, not less than 5 psig
questions.why: The test is at least 1.5 x working pressure and never below 3 psig.

questions.q: Minimum gas pressure test duration for a single-family dwelling:
questions.why: Single-family dwellings and systems under 10 cu ft: at least 10 minutes.

questions.q: Which test medium is prohibited for gas piping pressure tests?
questions.why: Oxygen may never be used to test gas piping.

questions.q: Minimum size of a CSST bonding conductor (copper):
questions.why: The CSST bonding conductor must be at least 6 AWG copper, no longer than 75 ft.

questions.q: An appliance gas shutoff valve must be within what distance of the appliance?
questions.why: The shutoff valve must be in the same room, within 6 ft.

questions.q: Maximum length of a gas appliance connector:
questions.why: Connectors may not exceed 6 ft, one per appliance.

questions.q: Minimum burial depth for underground gas piping (general):
questions.why: 12 in generally; 8 in for individual lines to outdoor appliances.

questions.q: Minimum size of the tracer wire for underground plastic gas pipe:
questions.why: A yellow insulated copper tracer at least 18 AWG is required.

questions.q: Shield plates for gas piping must extend at least how far above sole plates and below top plates?
questions.why: The IFGC requires 4 in, compared with 2 in in the IPC.

questions.q: Support spacing for 1/2 in steel gas pipe:
questions.why: 1/2 in steel: 6 ft; 3/4 to 1 in: 8 ft; 1-1/4 in and larger: 10 ft.

questions.q: The standard method for indoor combustion air requires how much room volume?
questions.why: The standard method requires 50 cu ft per 1,000 Btu/h of input.

questions.q: With two openings directly to the outdoors, each opening needs a free area of at least:
questions.why: Direct or vertical-duct openings need 1 sq in per 4,000 Btu/h each.

questions.q: If the free area of a wood louver is unknown, assume:
questions.why: Wood louvers are assumed 25% free area; metal louvers 75%.

questions.q: OSHA requires a ladder or other exit in trenches of what depth?
questions.why: Trenches 4 ft or deeper need egress within 25 ft of lateral travel.

questions.q: Maximum lateral travel distance to a means of egress in a trench:
questions.why: No more than 25 ft of lateral travel.

questions.q: A protective system is required in excavations at least how deep (unless in stable rock)?
questions.why: Protective systems are required at 5 ft or more.

questions.q: Maximum allowable slope for Type C soil:
questions.why: Type C is 1-1/2:1, Type B 1:1, Type A 3/4:1.

questions.q: Excavated spoil must be kept at least how far from the edge of the trench?
questions.why: Spoil and equipment stay at least 2 ft from the edge.

questions.q: Sloping systems for excavations deeper than what depth must be designed by a registered professional engineer?
questions.why: Excavations over 20 ft deep need an engineered design.

questions.q: Type A soil has an unconfined compressive strength of at least:
questions.why: Type A is 1.5 tsf or more; Type C is 0.5 tsf or less.

questions.q: How many gallons does 1 ft of 4 in pipe hold (approximately)?
questions.why: 0.0408 x 4 squared = 0.653 gallons per foot.

questions.q: Pressure created by each foot of water head:
questions.why: 1 ft of water = 0.433 psi; 1 psi = 2.31 ft.

questions.q: What static pressure exists at the bottom of a 100 ft column of water?
For a 45-degree offset of 20 in, the travel (center to center) is about:
questions.why: Travel = offset x 1.414 = 20 x 1.414 = 28.3 in.

questions.q: A slope of 1/4 in per ft is approximately what percent grade?
How much does 60 ft of drain fall at 1/4 in per ft?
questions.why: 60 x 0.25 = 15 in of total fall.

questions.q: How many gallons are in one cubic foot of water?
questions.why: 1 cu ft = 7.48 gallons; water weighs 8.34 lb per gallon.

questions.q: A rectangular tank 5 ft long x 2 ft wide x 3 ft high holds about how many gallons?
questions.why: 5 x 2 x 3 = 30 cu ft x 7.48 = 224.4 gallons.

questions.q: About how much does 10 gallons of water weigh?
Minimum shower compartment area under the UPC:
questions.why: The UPC requires 1,024 sq in and a 30 in circle; the IPC requires 900 sq in.

questions.q: Clear space required in front of a water closet under the UPC:
questions.why: UPC 24 in versus IPC 21 in.

questions.q: Maximum trap arm length for a 1-1/2 in trap under the UPC:
questions.why: UPC 1-1/2 in trap arm = 3 ft 6 in; the IPC allows 6 ft.

questions.q: Under the UPC, a relief valve drain run outside must end how far above the ground?
c: Between 6 in and 2 ft, pointing down
questions.why: The UPC requires termination 6 in to 2 ft above grade, pointing downward.
